articles.title: Telangana steps up game on food safety, cancels 30 licences in 1 month
articles.summary: Responding to queries from TOI readers, Avinash Mohanty, commissioner, TG SAFE, says the dept inspected 208 establishments since August, flagging
articles.body: Responding to queries from TOI readers, Avinash Mohanty, commissioner, TG SAFE, says the dept inspected 208 establishments since August, flagging violations ranging from poor hygiene to sale of analogue paneer and substandard medicines.Many edible items are being adulterated. What is being done to ensure such products do not flood the market?— Gura Prasad AchantaWe conduct regular drives to ascertain the quality of food products and check for adulteration. Since the formation of TG SAFE in August, special drives have been conducted on manufacturing and retailers of sweets, khoya, paneer and other dairy products. In the recent drive, 46 establishments were inspected. The licences of four establishments were suspended for serious violations, and more than 19 tonnes of material were seized. Orders have also recently been issued prohibiting the manufacture, storage, transport and sale of analogue paneer in Telangana.How does TG SAFE check whether medicines sold in pharmacies are genuine and meet quality standards?— Shrihari YJust like food outlets, pharmacies and wholesalers are also inspected. Samples are collected and sent to the Drugs Control Laboratory under TG SAFE, for analysis. Since January 2025, 115 medicines have been detected as Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). Various actions, including prosecution and suspension or cancellation of licences, are taken under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act.If a medicine is found to be substandard or unsafe after reaching the market, how is it recalled, and how are consumers alerted?— M UshaMedicines are sampled based on a risk-based approach, manpower and logistical availability, and other relevant factors. If a medicine sample is found to be substandard or unsafe by the laboratory, it is recalled by issuing necessary orders through the licensing authorities of the Drug Control Administraion.Is there a need for more food safety officers in the state? How many samples are tested monthly?— Chada Rekha RaoTG SAFE has recently been formed by merging the Food Safety Wings of GHMC and the Institute of Preventive Medicine. We are currently assessing the manpower requirements across all wings of the dept and will take up the requirements with the govt. At present, nearly 500–600 food samples are sent for laboratory testing every month, and we aim to substantially increase this number.What do officials check during inspections?— Balamukund During inspections, Food Safety Officers check overall food hygiene and safety, including the condition of the premises, personal hygiene of food handlers, storage and temperature control, raw materials, cleanliness, pest control labelling and records. The handling and disposal of food waste and leftovers are also covered as part of hygiene and sanitation requirements, particularly to ensure that waste does not contaminate food or create conditions for pest infestation.If several people fall sick after eating at the same restaurant or consuming the same food product, what should they do?— Nithin ReddyThey should immediately complain to TG SAFE through the channels mentioned in the queries. TG SAFE will have the matter investigated and, if the samples are found to be unsafe, take appropriate action. Punishments are stringent if unsafe food causes people to fall sick.Should palm oil, food colors or other substances be banned? How can reuse of cooking oil be controlled?— Dr AM DayalPalm oil is permitted within India’s food regulatory framework. Certain natural and synthetic colours are permitted for specified foods and within prescribed limits. Unauthorised colours are not permitted and are checked during inspections. With regard to used cooking oil, an important parameter is Total Polar Compounds (TPC), which should be within permissible limits. Cooking oil with TPC above 25% should not be used for frying and must be discarded appropriately.What happened to the Hygiene Rating system? How many eateries have been rated?—Keerthana MThe FSSAI Hygiene Rating Scheme continues to be operational and provides consumers with information on the hygiene standards of participating food establishments. In Telangana, around 609 food business operators (FBOs) have received hygiene ratings so far. We are encouraging more eligible establishments to participate.Even now, many restaurants do not allow customers to check their kitchens. Can this be made mandatory, if a customer requests?—Vilas PenurkarThe power to enter and inspect a food establishment is a statutory power granted to the authorities under the Food Safety and Standards Act. While the Act provides for a customer to get a food sample analysed to check its quality, there is no provision under the Act granting customers the right to check kitchens. However, we will examine with FSSAI whether checking of kitchens by customers in certain situations can be made possible.Can you make risk-based inspections and surprise sampling compulsory? Can mobile laboratories be increased?— CS BansalWe have been conducting risk-based inspections and sampling through special drives targeting specific food categories and establishments based on identified risks. Recent drives have covered meat, spices, sweets and milk products, edible oils, cereals and other food businesses.Surprise inspections and sampling are also undertaken as part of these enforcement activities. Mobile food-testing laboratories will be expanded to support rapid field-level screening, with suspected or non-compliant samples being referred to notified laboratories for detailed analysis. They will be increased as per the requirement.Can CCTV cameras be mandatory in restaurants? Can only branded/high-quality raw materials be mandated?— Madhav Sagar VVAt present, the Food Safety and Standards Act does not specifically mandate CCTV cameras in restaurants. However, the possibility of making CCTV coverage mandatory for certain categories of high-risk or large food establishments may be examined.Similarly, restaurants cannot be required to use only branded raw materials. The requirement is that all ingredients comply with the applicable FSSAI standards.Can TG SAFE address long storage of masalas, gravies and prepared foods?— Rajesh MehataStorage of prepared foods, masalas and gravies is an important food-safety requirement and is checked during inspections. Officials check storage conditions, temperature, shelf life and hygiene. Where there is a suspicion of non-compliance, samples are collected and sent for laboratory analysis.At present, there is no provision for a mandatory monthly food-safety certificate for eateries. FSSAI's existing Hygiene Rating Scheme provides a mechanism for assessing and displaying the hygiene and food-safety compliance of food establishments.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: UK military jamming other nations' satellites to defend itself, BBC told
articles.summary: The head of the RAF says the UK faces "unprecedented threats" from adversaries in space, as a new unit is created to defend Britain's satellites.
articles.body:
The British military has been jamming or blocking satellites from other countries in order to defend itself from hostile threats, the BBC has been told.

The RAF has been using a ground-based system for the past year, which a defence source said had already been used "to deter our adversaries".

It is understood the system could be used to prevent a hostile nation's satellites from tracking the movement of the UK's nuclear armed submarines or other sensitive military operations, such as those involving special forces.

It comes as the head of the RAF said the UK faced "unprecedented threats" from adversaries in space, coinciding with the creation of a new RAF unit set up to defend Britain's satellites.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) said the new Space Effects Squadron will be focused on "disrupting, degrading and denying hostile threats in space".

In a speech on Wednesday, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said daily lives depend on satellites that power everyday technologies like mobile phones and banking apps, adding the loss of GPS would cost the UK economy £1.4bn a day.

"Our dependency on space is precisely why it is increasingly under threat from our adversaries." he said.

"We depend on them for everything from weather forecasts, energy supplies, and financial transactions to sat-navs, mobile phone connections, and Amazon deliveries," said Streeting, adding that the loss of "everyday conveniences would undermine our daily freedoms, and trust in our institutions."

Speaking at the UK Space Conference, Streeting said that threat from Britain's adversaries was growing in "scale, speed and sophistication", adding that the "challenges in space increasingly mirror the geopolitics on Earth".

A number of nations are believed to have similar ground-based systems against satellites. Last year the then head the UK's Space Command said Russia was trying to jam UK satellites with ground based systems "every week" .

The defence source described the UK's terrestrial electronic warfare capability as "world leading, and more".

Last week US confirmed for the first time that it had also deployed an unspecified "weapon" in space to defend its own satellites.

Both China and Russia condemned the move - warning of an arms race in space.

However, Washington has already accused both Russian and China of developing their own space weapons - ranging from electronic jammers, lasers to blind other satellites and even projectiles that can be fired from satellites in orbit.

In May, the RAF tracked a series of "dangerous manoeuvres" by five Russian satellites moving close to two Finnish commercial satellites. The RAF's Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth said in June that a Russian satellite constellation had caused disruptions to GPS signals across Europe and Canada.

The UK has a handful of military satellites in orbit for surveillance and military communications. But it works closely with the US Space Force - which has many more.

In a separate speech at the space conference, ACM Smyth added that "unfortunately we are seeing more and more irresponsible and provocative actions from our adversaries".

ACM Smyth warned that without satellites, some of the technologies people take for granted would be lost and would make every sector "less efficient, less prosperous and less secure".

"Sat-nav systems would fail, congestion on our roads would be severe and our emergency services would take longer to help those in need," he said, adding that satellites are also needed to monitor the weather and the effects of climate change.

articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Minnesota GOP candidates keep Trump at arm's length as they eye a post-Trump party future
articles.summary: Michele Tafoya and Lisa Demuth navigate a tricky balance on Trump in Minnesota, embracing some policies while keeping the president at arm's length.
articles.body: As the once-long shot Minnesota GOP Senate nominee Michele Tafoya has closed in on Democratic opponent Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, the issue of President Donald Trump — who is not particularly popular in the Gopher State — has taken a unique turn. For Tafoya, as well as gubernatorial candidate Lisa Demuth and others down ballot for the GOP — not to mention their potential voters — the general attitude toward Trump is that while they support much of what he has done, they also represent what a post-Donald Trump Republican Party could look like. This week in St. Cloud, I met John, who was sitting in his SUV outside the courthouse. Covered in pro-Trump stickers and flags, the vehicle served as a kind of quiet, solo demonstration. I mentioned to him that his "Trump 2028" flag, in particular, seemed a bit provocative. He told me, "Well, I know he’s not really going to run again, I don’t think he legally can, but that’s just more for comedy and just for fun," adding that he thinks Vice President JD Vance is a great choice to run next, perhaps with Secretary of State Marco Rubio as his running mate. When I asked whether he thought that Tafoya and Demuth should embrace Trump more, John told me, "That's the problem with Minnesota [Republicans]. We need to be hardcore Trump, not lukewarm, and I think that’s kind of biting them in the butt, they've got to be all in." Bob, who I had chatted with the night before, along with his wife Mary, was a counterpoint that showed the eye of the needle the Minnesota GOP needs to thread. He’s retired from banking and is now a soybean farmer with mixed and nuanced views on Trump and especially his tariff regime. "The tariffs hurt us," Bob confided to Fox News Digital, but added that "the administration provided subsidies, we got about $40,000 last year that helped us stay afloat." But Bob also pointed out that things weren’t perfect before the tariffs, when it seemed countries like China were simply taking advantage of American farmers. Likewise, Scott, a man in his 60s, who I met as he was walking his dog amid the pretty, old brick buildings of solid Midwestern St. Cloud, is far from a Trump supporter, but is considering the GOP this year because of the Somali fraud scandal, which he said he has seen close up in his town. "They don’t work," Scott scoffed, before adding, "But you see them in these shiny new cars, we all knew something was going on way before it hit the news, it was just obvious." PEGGY FLANAGAN WAS MINNESOTA'S NO 2 OFFICIAL AS MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL EXPLODED UNDER STATE'S WATCH The Somali fraud question can cut both ways, though, as the manager of the restaurant where I had lunch made clear. He told me that the crackdown in St. Cloud was "extreme," and that he rarely protests, but did in this case, getting pepper sprayed for his trouble. But, when I asked if the enforcement has been less aggressive over the past few months, he was quick to admit that, "Yes, it has calmed down a lot." When you put the above pieces of the Minnesota electoral mosaic together, it becomes clear why it behooves Tafoya and Demuth to keep Trump at arm’s length, without fully breaking with him: to embrace clear successes like the closed-up southern border and no tax on overtime, while questioning less popular measures such as tariffs and the Iran war. And, after all, should Tafoya win, her four or six-year term will be under a president who is not Trump. Likewise, should Demuth serve two terms in the governor’s mansion, six of the eight years will see a new resident at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. DAVID MARCUS: IN DEEP BLUE MINNESOTA A RED DAWN MAY BE RISING AHEAD OF THE MIDTERMS Gentle pushback on the POTUS is becoming something of a national trend for GOP Senate candidates, with both Michigan’s Mike Rogers and Iowa’s Ashley Hinson calling this week for an abrupt end to Trump’s military actions in Iran. Just as was true at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas two weeks ago. The firm subtext of the tight races this year is: What comes after Donald Trump? With the Democratic Party hurtling toward socialism all over the map, many Republicans think Tafoya is a sensible centrist who can grow the brand over the next decade. NEWT GINGRICH: REPUBLICANS CAN WIN THE 2026 MIDTERMS — IF THEY FOLLOW THE PLAN For their part, expect Democrats in Minnesota like Flanagan and Sen. Amy Klobuchar, who is running for governor, to keep pounding away at Trump like Rocky attacking Apollo Creed’s midsection. They seek anything but a nuanced and thoughtful race — they just want rage against the "orange man." articles.title: Family 'heartbroken' after mother and three children died in fire
articles.summary: Elisha Brabin, 36, and her children, Leo, 16, Ellis, 8, and Prudence, 7, died in Bootle on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The family of a mother and three children who died in a house fire have said they are experiencing an "unimaginable" loss.

Elisha Brabin, 36, and her children, Leo, 16, Ellis, 8, and Prudence, 7, died after a blaze "spread rapidly" inside a house on Stone Square in Bootle, Merseyside, in the early hours of Tuesday.

Paying tribute, their relatives said they had been left "heartbroken" and the loss would be "felt forever".

The statement added that "Elisha was a devoted and loving mother" and "our beautiful babies, Leo, Ellis and Prudence, were loved beyond measure".

The family said they were "devastated by the loss of Elisha, Leo, Ellis and Prudence".

"Elisha was our beloved daughter, wife, mother, sister, auntie, niece and cousin," they said.

"She was a devoted and loving mother who lived for her children. They were her whole world, and she meant everything to us."

The statement added: "Our beautiful babies, Leo, Ellis and Prudence, were loved beyond measure and brought so much joy, happiness and love to our family.

"They filled our lives with laughter and precious memories that we will cherish forever.

"The tragic loss of Elisha and our three precious children has left us heartbroken. They have all been taken from us far too soon.

"The loss we are experiencing is unimaginable, and the impact on our family will be felt forever."

The family asked for privacy whilst they grieved and supported one another, adding: "We would like to thank everyone for their kindness, support and understanding."

Rachel, who grew up near the mother, told the BBC: "She made her children happy, she did everything for her children." She added: "They were loved. It's just really, really sad."

After leaving flowers close to a police cordon around Stone Square, she said: "Even if I didn't know her, I'd still be here paying my respects because the young children have lost their lives and so has the mother.

Loti Nambombe, who is taking care of the family's dog after the fire, said: "It's a community. It's broken. It hurts."

Nambombe set up an online fundraising page for the family, which had raised more than £5,000 on Wednesday.

He said: "Everybody just wants to do something to help, that's our duty as neighbours and as a community."

He said funds could go towards funeral costs or anything else the family needed.

Nambombe told how residents came out in the street to help after hearing screaming when the blaze broke out.

He said: "Some of the guys here are real heroes. They were trying to run in, get ladders or smash windows to get people out. People nearly risked their own lives to try and help."

Speaking to BBC Radio Merseyside, Liverpool metro mayor Steve Rotheram said: "There is that bond in most of those communities that we're talking about, certainly in Bootle and places like that - a very, very strong identity.

"I'm certain that whatever they can do as a community to help those who have been left behind, they will."

articles.title: ‘People of Russia support our efforts’: Putin says record turnout shows Russians back his military agenda in Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday said high voter turnout in the country's parliamentary election showed public support for his policies and
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday said high voter turnout in the country's parliamentary election showed public support for his policies and for the armed forces fighting in Ukraine, after preliminary results gave his United Russia party a record parliamentary majority.More than 97% of the votes had been counted, with United Russia expected to win more than three-fourths of the 450 seats in the State Duma, according to election officials cited by news agency AP.Near-complete results showed the party securing 355 seats, or nearly 80% of the lower house, after winning more than 57% of the vote.The election, held over three days from September 18 to 20, was the first parliamentary poll since Putin launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.It was also the first to include residents of four Ukrainian regions that Russia seized and declared annexed later that year. Ukraine has rejected the voting in those territories as illegal.Putin links turnout to support for war effortPutin, speaking publicly about the results for the first time, said turnout demonstrated support for the government's policies.“Such a high, even record, number of people who came out and voted shows that the people of Russia support our efforts aimed at strengthening the country,” he said, according to Reuters.Russia's Central Electoral Commission put turnout at 59.3%, while AP reported that turnout exceeded 59% of the 111 million eligible voters, making it the highest for a parliamentary election in more than a decade.Putin also directly addressed Russian troops fighting in Ukraine.“This vote is for you. People believe in you, believe in our victory, believe in your courage, in your heroism,” he said.Putin further said, “I have no doubt that all the goals we set for the special military operation will be fulfilled,” using the Kremlin's term for the war.Voting held amid Ukrainian drone attacksThe election took place amid continued Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia.Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down 1,110 drones overnight on Sunday. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 450 drones targeting the capital were downed in what he described as the city's “largest ever” attack.Officials said the attacks damaged an oil refinery and a residential building and killed three people and injured 38 in the wider Moscow region.“They tried to hamper our efforts, to derail the election, as evidenced by the enemy’s continuous efforts to breach air defenses around Moscow and in other regions,” Putin said.“But lines at polling stations have shown that Russia can’t be intimidated.”Authorities extended voting to three days and used online voting in some regions. Voting was also held in Crimea, which Russia annexed in 2014, and in the four Ukrainian regions claimed by Moscow.United Russia set for record majorityPreliminary results indicated that United Russia would win between 347 and 355 seats. The party secured just under 58% of the party-list vote for 225 seats and won 208 single-seat constituencies, which make up the other half of the Duma.Several smaller parties that form Russia's “systemic opposition” are expected to take most of the remaining seats. Only a small number are expected to go to candidates who ran without party affiliation.The liberal Yabloko party, which had publicly criticised the war, was removed from the ballot by Russia's Supreme Court last month and had only a limited number of candidates in single-seat contests.Preliminary results showed that none of its candidates had won a seat.The election was conducted under extensive state media coverage and tight political controls, while voting also took place in territories whose annexation by Russia has been rejected by Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.title: Board of Peace plans $2.4bn Gaza reconstruction as Israel kills seven
articles.summary: Violations against Palestinians in Gaza continue even as world leaders call on Israel to adhere to ceasefire deal.
articles.body:
The United States-backed Board of Peace has proposed a $2.4bn plan to begin reconstruction in the Gaza Strip, even as Israeli attacks kill seven Palestinians across the enclave.

The body tasked with overseeing the ceasefire and Gaza’s reconstruction unveiled on Wednesday a 66-project blueprint at a meeting of the group’s board on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

The full cost of the reconstruction from the damage inflicted on Gaza by Israeli attacks is expected to cost about $35bn over the medium term and an additional $71.4bn in the next 10 years, according to the Board of Peace plan.

The Board of Peace’s high representative, Nikolay Mladenov, said the proposed plan depends on Hamas’s disarmament.

Hamas and other Palestinian factions in July agreed to a document setting out a plan for their disarmament in Gaza, in what United States President Donald Trump has called “a monumental step” towards peace and security.

“I want to be very clear that we are not bound by a calendar,” Mladenov said. “We want to make sure that this works.”

Reporting from the Board of Peace news conference in New York, Al Jazeera’s Kristen Saloomey said “little progress has been made on the ground” in Gaza. “What we’ve been hearing from the experts in this meeting is what a daunting task is ahead,” she said.

While efforts to alleviate the dire conditions in Gaza were endorsed by the international community in July, “Israel has not lived up to its commitment to withdraw its troops on the ground, and so recovery really has yet to begin,” she said.

On Wednesday, an Israeli drone attack on a vehicle in the al-Mawasi area near the city of Khan Younis in the south of the coastal enclave killed two people. Medics identified the dead as Osama Abu Khater and Mohammad Abu Elwan.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in a statement that the attack had killed a senior Hamas finance official.

Reporting from Gaza City, Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim Al Khalili said that “the situation is going from bad to worse in the wake of these Israeli attacks.”

The attacks are happening near “displacement camps where hundreds of thousands of Palestinians sought refuge, believing that these tents will offer them a sense of normalcy and safety, but ended up being affected by these ongoing ceasefire violations”, he added.

An aerial attack on another vehicle in central Gaza’s Deir el-Balah killed at least two Palestinians, and an additional strike in Gaza City killed at least one more.

A man and a woman also succumbed to wounds sustained from Israeli gunfire in previous days. In Khan Younis, an infant and an elderly woman were both wounded by Israeli gunfire in separate incidents.

Israel’s routine violations in Gaza and the occupied West Bank have drawn a string of condemnations from world leaders convening for UNGA.

On Tuesday, the leaders of the United Kingdom, France and Canada criticised Israel for blocking a two-state solution through its policy of illegal settlement in the West Bank and said that the suffering in Gaza had to be alleviated.

UN chief Antonio Guterres denounced Israel’s actions in the Palestinian enclave, adding that “the United Nations need to be allowed to perform our mandates in Gaza.”

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan reaffirmed his country’s commitment to the Gaza ceasefire agreement as a signatory, demanding that reconstruction of the devastated territory must start “as soon as possible”.

articles.title: 'Nagarjuna is an H-1B trafficker': Sara Gonzales claims Indian techie hirer she exposed earlier is now selling home, going back to India
articles.summary: In May this year, Texas journalist Sara Gonzales picked up an alleged H-1B abuse case by one Nagarjuna Reddy Sakam, who made plenty of hires through his
articles.body: In May this year, Texas journalist Sara Gonzales picked up an alleged H-1B abuse case by one Nagarjuna Reddy Sakam, who made plenty of hires through his company 'Great America Technologies'. Gonzales, at that time, knocked on Reddy's door, and their altercation went viral. Nagarjuna said he was not doing anything illegal, but Gonzales insisted that she had many tips against him. Four months after the first video, Gonzales dropped a follow-up on that video, claiming that Nagarjuna was selling his house and was going back to India. There is, however, no official confirmation of the man going back to India. Gonzales, in her latest video, showed that the house was listed for sale.Gonzales said that after her first video, many whistleblowers contacted her and they said that Nagarjuna did not pay them for months. Nagarjuna's company is a third-party staffing company that handles H-1B hiring for IT companies.One Indian whistleblower said he paid $6k to $7k to one such consultancy firm in the name of attorney fees and said he was unaware that candidates were not supposed to pay any fee for the H-1B sponsorship. The man said the consultancy promised that they would pay back the money after six months or one year. The man said that, as he was unhappy with the consultancy that originally sponsored him, he came under Nagarjuna's consultancy. The man said he got to know about Nagarjuna from the Indian community in Frisco.But the issue was the same with Nagarjuna's consultancy as well. The man said he was not paid for months, and when he asked for his salary, Nagarjuna blocked him. Gonzales pointed out that Nagarjuna took PPP loans to cover payroll, but he was not paying at all.The whistleblower said he learned that after Gonzales' video, Nagarjuna was not in the US for two months -- probably in India. "He came back a few days ago," the man said.Gonzales again paid a visit to Nagarjuna's address but could not get any response from Nagarjuna. She believed that the house was being shown for sale, and she also found the listing. In the video, she took out a loudspeaker and announced to the neighborhood that Nagarjuna is an H-1B trafficker.
